dimoose: read, build, check, prune and share dichotomous keys

Source: R/dimoose-package.R
dimoose-package.Rd

A dichotomous key identifies a specimen by a series of choices. dimoose keeps a key as a dimoose object, a table of couplets and leads, and provides the tools around it. key$validate() checks any key, however it was made.

Where to start

  • Write a key in a spreadsheet and read it with keyFromSpreadsheet(); keyToSpreadsheet() writes any key back out for editing. montanaKey(), sharkKey(), arachnidaKey(), vibrioKey() and phylotreeKey() are example keys.

  • Read a key somebody else wrote: plain text as printed in a flora (keyFromText(), parseTextKey()), FishBase (importFishbase()), or the keys and character matrices of other identification software (readSDD(), readSDDKey(), readDELTA(), readLucid(), readLucidKey(), readXper(), each with a writer).

  • Check it: checkNames() looks its names up in GBIF, and summary() and keyQuality() say how many steps it takes to reach a result, optionally weighted by how common each taxon is (occurrenceWeights()).

  • Cut it down or join keys up: pruneKey() keeps or drops taxa, regionalKey() keeps the taxa recorded in a place, and mergeKeys() grafts one key onto a result of another.

  • Generate a key from data: from a character matrix (keyFromMatrix(), or generateTree() with keyFromRpart()), from a sequence alignment (keyFromAlignment()), or from labelled photos with a vision model (visionModel(), embedImages(), discoverSniglets(), keyFromSniglets(), keyFromClusters()). Such keys can be followed by machine with classify() and tested with evaluateKey() and benchmarkKey().

  • Share it: exportWizard() writes a self-contained web page that works on a phone, keyDiagram() draws a box diagram, and toNewick(), toIgraph(), toTreedata() and toAuspiceJSON() hand the key to phylogenetics software.

Vignettes

  • vignette("montana-hardwoods", package = "dimoose"): a key written in a spreadsheet, with photos.

  • vignette("published-key", package = "dimoose"): from a printed key to a regional key on a phone.

  • vignette("vision-keys", package = "dimoose"): keys from photos.

  • vignette("alignment-keys", package = "dimoose"): keys from aligned sequences.

Web services and optional software

Reading, building, checking and exporting keys needs nothing beyond the packages dimoose imports. checkNames(), regionalKey(), occurrenceWeights(), importFishbase() and inatPhotos() ask public web services (GBIF, iNaturalist, FishBase) and need an internet connection. The vision functions run a model in Python through the reticulate package, which sets Python up on first use; saveEmbeddings() and loadEmbeddings() let the later steps run without it.
